subject: Post-demo: caching strategy & target unit cost for Stellara pilot
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@stellara.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: caching strategy & target unit cost for Stellara pilot

Hi Emma — thanks again for the demo time earlier today. Quick recap and the immediate asks we agreed on: 

Summary from our side:
- Objective: pilot Redwood inference behind Stellara's conversational triage to assess latency, reliability, and effective unit cost to guide procurement.
- Key metric you called out: target effective price per 1M tokens for budget approval (you mentioned a target range at the end of the call).
- Main levers we discussed: model selection, batching, and caching (prefix/prefetch).

Action items for you (if possible):
1) Confirm expected monthly token volume (range is fine: e.g., 5M–25M / month).
2) Tell us whether traffic is steady or highly spiky (support windows / nightly batches).
3) Confirm the target $/1M tokens you'd want us to aim for for pilot approval (ballpark is ok).

What we'll deliver (next from Redwood):
- A short worked example showing effective $/1M at a few cache hit rates (0%, 30%, 60%) plus simple assumptions for prefix vs full-response caching.
- A lightweight traffic capture recipe (7-day sample) and a simulated costing spreadsheet so you can vary hit rates and volumes.

Attached: stellara-econ-worksheet.xlsx (workbook with placeholders)

Notes on caching assumptions we discussed:
- Prefix caching (cache the first N tokens of common prompts) tends to increase hit rate for multi-turn flows where users ask similar starters.
- Prefetching: precompute likely next-turn completions on session creation — helps reduce cold-starts for high-frequency users but increases write/compute upfront.
- Tradeoffs: higher prefetch aggressiveness increases cache hit rate but increases write/compute and storage overheads; eviction policy matters for noisy traffic.

Would you be able to share a rough volume range and whether your pilot is intended to run 24/7 or on business hours only? If you prefer, I can prepare the worked examples against two volume scenarios.

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa and Ben for the worked economics.

—Connor

Connor — thanks for the recap and fast follow. A few points from our side: 

Volumes: 
- Expected pilot traffic: ~8M tokens/month initially, ramp to ~18–22M over 60 days if signal looks good.
- Traffic profile: mostly business hours (US Eastern) with small evening activity; bursts after newsletter drops (~3x baseline for 2–3 hours).

Target price:
- Our procurement team is comfortable reviewing a vendor if the effective cost is under $200 / 1M tokens (pilot target).

Security & compliance:
- We will need SOC2 evidence as part of procurement; if you can share a pointer to your current attestation that helps.

Requested worked examples:
- Can you show effective $/1M at these hit rates: 0%, 30%, 50%? Also useful to see a worked example for a prefetch scenario where we precompute first-turn completions for the top 15% of sessions.

Attached: current-query-sample.json (small sample of typical user prompts and average token lengths)

Thanks — happy to jump on another 30-minute sync once you send the worked examples.

—Emma

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Post-demo: caching strategy & target unit cost for Stellara pilot

Folks — I drafted the worked examples Emma asked for and attached a simple CSV so we can iterate. Below is a short explanation + numbers using conservative assumptions so procurement sees downside.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Baseline inference compute cost (hosted model, medium-size LLM): $250 per 1M tokens served (this reflects model/infra only; discounts or dedicated pricing will change this).
- Cache read cost (serving from prefix/response cache): $10 per 1M tokens (storage + small I/O).
- "Hit rate" defined as fraction of tokens served from cache (not fraction of requests).
- Prefetch overhead: assume 0.15 extra compute tokens per session for prefetch write cost when prefetching top flows (counts as compute, not cached).

Worked examples — effective cost per 1M tokens (formula: effective = base*(1 - hit) + cache_cost*hit + prefetch_overhead_cost when applicable):
- 0% hit: effective = $250 (no cache benefit)
- 30% hit: effective = 250*0.7 + 10*0.3 = 175 + 3 = $178 per 1M
- 50% hit: effective = 250*0.5 + 10*0.5 = 125 + 5 = $130 per 1M
- 60% hit: effective = 250*0.4 + 10*0.6 = 100 + 6 = $106 per 1M

Prefetch scenario (top 15% sessions prefetched):
- Prefetch adds compute overhead equivalent to ~0.15 M tokens per 1M user tokens (i.e., 15% of sessions each incur ~0.15 M extra tokens worth of compute during prefetch warmup). That maps to an added ~$37.50 per 1M (0.15 * $250).
- Example: 50% hit with prefetch overhead: base*(1 - hit) + cache_cost*hit + prefetch_cost = 125 + 5 + 37.5 = $167.5 per 1M
- Interpretation: prefetch helps increase hit rate (e.g., 50% -> 65% for a common flow), but you must model the upfront prefetch cost. If prefetch moves 50% -> 65% and prefetch overhead is 0.15, the math becomes: 250*(1-0.65) + 10*0.65 + 0.15*250 = 87.5 + 6.5 + 37.5 = $131.5 per 1M — still net positive vs no prefetch in that case.

Other notes:
- Hit rates are workload-dependent. Bot-style repetitive prompts can hit >70% with prefix caching; open-ended QA tends to stay low.
- Eviction windows: for an active user base, a 24–72 hour TTL on prefix cache often gives most of the benefit without ballooning storage.
- For spikes (newsletter), caching reduces incremental cost significantly since repeated post prompts reuse similar prefixes.

I've attached stellara-cache-modeling-v1.csv — it has the formulas and you can plug in your volumes and preferred hit rates. Happy to adjust the base cost if Connor gets input from procurement on acceptable baseline discounts.

Next steps I propose:
1) Connor: ask Emma for a 7-day traffic dump (anonymized) or let us run a 7-day proxy capture with the sample file.
2) Redwood: we run the CSV against the sample and return a short memo with two pricing options: managed hosted pilot (no commitment) and a committed pilot rate (1–3mo, volume-based discount).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@stellara.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Post-demo: caching strategy & target unit cost for Stellara pilot

Emma — appreciate the clarity on target. Quick confirmations and a proposed next step: 

1) We can hit an effective $150 / 1M tokens for the pilot if we model a 50% sustained hit rate and offer a pilot discount on the baseline compute line (we'd set baseline internal price to $220/1M for the pilot). That maps to: 220*0.5 + 10*0.5 = $115 + $5 = $120; with a conservative pilot admin surcharge we’d list $150 as the effective price for procurement paperwork.

2) If your traffic stays at 8M -> ramp to 20M / month, we recommend a 60-day pilot with a usage review at 30 days to validate hit rate assumptions.

3) Next steps: Connor — can you send the sample capture recipe + the updated CSV to Emma and the procurement contact so they can start an internal ticket? Emma — if you can drop the contact for procurement (name/email), we’ll include the SOC2 link and a one-page pilot SOW.

Thanks — happy to join a procurement call if needed.

—Ben
